newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Oct 7.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Oct 7.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian driver Craig Lowndes, 22, yesterday became the youngest ever winner of the Bathurst 1000, along with his New Zealand co-driver Greg Murphy, after former World Formula One champion Alan Jones was forced to withdraw as his car caught fire. Page 1

According to leading lawyers, sporting organisations will face increased scrutiny under the Trade Practices Act from now on due to a decision by the Full Federal Court to grant Super League the right to organise its own rugby league games. Page 1.

The future of the Australian Rugby League was in the hands of television magnate Kerry Packer, who holds the free-to-air rights to ARL games and who persuaded the ARL clubs to reject the original approaches from Super League, and the subscription televisin provider Optus Vision, who has announced its continuing support for the ARL despite the Super League green light, as the prospect of immediate talks with Super League faded. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian rookie Karrie Webb ground out a closing two-over-par 73 on the Wykagyl Country Club at New Rochelle to share second place with American Tina Barrett in the Big Apple Classic behind England's Caroline Pierce. Page 30.

Australian batsman Michael Bevan has increased his chances for inclusion in next week's Test match against India after making a century in the three-day tour match against a President's XI on Sunday. Bevan made a century from 157 balls and looks ready to break back into test cricket following a two-year absence since the 1994-95 England tour. Page 22.

Australian Rugby Union great David Campese has made an impassioned plea to administrators to allow representative players to continue appearing for their club sides. Campese, Australia's most capped Test representative, said he was concerned the Australia Rugby Football Union was becoming protective of contracted players. Page 23.
THE AGE

Twenty-five-year-old Melbourne golfer Robert Allenby is lucky to be alive after crashing through a roundabout in the Spanish Costa del Sol last weekend. The crash means he will be unable to take on Greg Norman and Tiger Woods at next month's Australian Open. Page A1.

The National Basketball League's Brisbane Bullets dampened the Melbourne Tigers' championship hopes after they defeated the team 118-97 in their first quarter-final over the weekend. The result means the Tigers cannot afford to drop tonight's game at Melbourne Park, and must win the deciding game on Wednesday night to stay in contention. Page 5.

Collingwood Warriors had a near win over traditional power Marconi in soccer's National Cup final yesterday. The 1-0 match attracted a large crowd at Bob Jane Stadium to see the Warriors begin their 1996 campaign with the first trophy of the national league season. Page 12.
HERALD SUN

Australian Rugby League club St George will meet this week to discuss survival options, including relocating to Melbourne, in the wake of last week's ruling to allow News Limited to run a Superleague competition. The meeting will address the club's long-term viability, possible mergers and becoming a Victorian franchise. Page 78.

Former Australian Football League's Hawthorn premiership full-back Kevin Moore has returned to Glenferrie as chairman of selectors in the aftermath of the failed merger. Former Demon recruiting manager Cameron Schwab is also being considered for a return as part of sweeping changes to the club's administration. Page 78.

One of Australia's best jockeys, Mick Dittman, has replaced Kevin Forrester as rider of Dupain in this year's Caulfield and Melbourne Cups. Forrester was outed for ten days after he was suspended for his ride on Gossips in the Shannon Quality. Page 76.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

The controversial Federal Court decision in favour of News Ltd's Superleague will enable the rebel competition to revolutionise the game, according to International Superleague Board chairman Maurice Lindsay. Lindsay said the decision had swept away a lot of confusion in the northern hemisphere and cleared the way for them to get on with plans. Page 23.

Superleague officials have revealed some changes to the current competition rules enforced by the Australian Rugby League. The new rules, to be implemented next season, will include scrums set in 20 metres from touch; no striking in the play-the-ball; givng players the incentive of a free tackle to pick up the ball instead of watching it roll out of touch; and having the scoring side kick off to restart play. Page 24.

It has been confirmed that Australian Football League's club Carlton want a Superleague club to be based at upgraded Optus Oval. Carlton general manager Stephen Gough said his club had registered the name Carlton Rugby League earlier this year when it lodged its national soccer league name. Page 24.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
